international.title: Iowa lead detonation: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite concerns - live updates
international.summary: The army plans to detonate of 68 barrels containing nearly 9,500lbs of lead azide despite public concern about potential health and environmental effects Sign up for the Breaking News US email The Iowa National Guard is providing up to 100 federally activated soldiers to support local, state and federal agencies in their public safety efforts around the controlled detonation. According to a news release from Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds, the soldiers will “assist with community outreach to approximately 150 households identified by local and federal authorities, providing official guidance and assistance to residents with the recommended temporary evacuation.” Muscatine, a town approximately 60 miles north of Middletown along the Mississippi River, was initially placed in the path of the plume by prediction models. Rehana Pasha, an employee at farm supply chain Blain’s Farm & Fleet, said she had been fielding questions from concerned farmers since the plans were first announced last week. She said supplies like containers to safely store water, tarps to cover livestock feed, and leaf-blowers to blow lead dust and other contaminants off surfaces had been selling fast. “Initially we had only five days of warning, and as a farm supply store we were overwhelmed with customers asking how to prepare,” she said, adding that their customer base skews older and was struggling to order supplies on Amazon and other e-commerce sites on such short notice.
